'''Vladimir Privman''' (2 January 1955 – 14 April 2018) was a professor of [[physics]] at [[Clarkson University]], where he held the Robert A. Plane Endowed Professorship. He also held joint appointments in the departments of [[Chemistry]] and [[Electrical and Computer Engineering]].<ref name="auto"/> He was best known for his work on bio-inspired information processing, synthesis of [[colloids]] and [[nanoparticles]], [[spintronics]] and [[quantum computing]], [[statistical mechanics]], [[polymer science]], and [[chemical kinetics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Vladimir Privman - US grants |url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/grants.php?pid=542848 |website=Academic Tree}}</ref> He also made numerous contributions to the field of [[unconventional computing]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Obituary for Professor Vladimir Privman |url=https://www.oldcitypublishing.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/11/IJUCv13n6p493-499Obituary.pdf}}</ref> In total, he authored over 250 academic papers and books.

Privman earned his doctorate in 1982 from [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|The Technion]]. He completed postdoctoral work at [[Cornell University]] and [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] before joining the faculty at [[Clarkson University]] in 1985. Early in his career, he received the [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]].<ref>{{cite web |title=ORCID |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5315-2604}}</ref> In 2006, he became a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], an honor bestowed on less than one-half of one percent of the society's membership.<ref name="auto"/> He was recognized for his "fundamental contributions and professional leadership in statistical physics, surface, colloid and polymer science, and quantum information science."<ref name="auto"/>
